question:
A 80-year-old woman is scheduled for femoral-popliteal bypass surgery. She has a history of
insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, and
stenting of the left anterior descending coronary artery 5 years ago. She states that she has had no
recent chest pain and can walk one block with a cane, limited by right leg claudication. Her current
medications are aspirin, rosuvastatin, atenolol, and insulin. Her heart rate is 58 beats per minute, and
her blood pressure is 104/86 mm Hg. She has no jugular venous distention, no murmurs, and no
lower-extremity edema. Peripheral pulses are barely detectable. An electrocardiogram is normal.
Which one of the following preoperative management approaches is most appropriate for this patient?
Answer Choices: (A) No additional assessment before surgery (B) Echocardiogram (C) 24-hour Holter
monitoring (D) Cardiac pharmacologic stress test (E) CT coronary calcium scoring (F) Nuclear
perfusion imaging (G) Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (H) Exercise stress test (I) Dobutamine stress
echocardiogram (J) Coronary angiography
 A. Dobutamine stress echocardiogram
B. 24-hour Holter monitoring
C. No additional assessment before surgery
D. Coronary angiography
E. Echocardiogram
F. CT coronary calcium scoring
G. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing
H. Exercise stress test
I. Nuclear perfusion imaging
J. Cardiac pharmacologic stress test
